query: For an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating susceptible to progressive plastic deformation during continuous loading, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain its creep resistance? Specify the governing factor and rationale, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, the operating boundaries under sustained stress, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: HVOF-sprayed FCC/BCC HEA coatings develop a refined microstructure with enhanced compressive residual stresses that inhibit dislocation mobility and delay progressive plastic deformation, thereby improving creep resistance under sustained loading.
generation.material_initial_state: HEA coatings deposited by conventional methods exhibiting coarser grain structures and minimal compressive stresses.
generation.intervention: Application of HVOF spraying deposition to form the protective HEA coating.
generation.conditions: Continuous mechanical loading at service-relevant temperatures, where sustained stress drives creep deformation.
generation.structural_mediator: Refined grain boundaries and induced compressive residual stress fields resulting from the high-velocity spraying process.
generation.mechanism: The HVOF process generates a non-equilibrium microstructure in the HEA coating that impedes dislocation movement by offering more effective barriers (grain boundaries and residual stress regions), thus reducing the rate of creep deformation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under identical loading and temperature conditions, HVOF-sprayed coatings will exhibit a lower strain rate and delayed onset of plastic deformation compared to coatings produced by conventional deposition techniques.
generation.baseline: The conventional HEA coating with a coarser microstructure and lower compressive residual stress serves as the starting point for comparison.
generation.boundary: The predicted improvement in creep resistance is expected to hold within the operational stress and temperature range typical for service conditions; deviations may occur at extreme temperatures or loads beyond the design limits.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of the improvement in creep resistance is uncertain due to variability in HVOF process parameters and the complex interplay of phase constituents in the HEA, necessitating quantification in controlled experiments.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a series of creep tests on two groups of HEA coatings: one group deposited by HVOF spraying and the other by conventional methods, ensuring identical chemical composition and baseline microstructural properties as starting references. Expose both groups to identical continuous loading at elevated temperatures while monitoring deformation over time.
measurements: Onset time for detectable plastic deformation
Microstructural analysis via electron microscopy to measure grain size and residual stress fields
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the HVOF-sprayed HEA coatings do not show a statistically significant reduction (e.g., at least a 20% decrease) in creep strain rate and delayed plastic deformation onset compared to the conventional coatings under the defined test conditions.

chosen.approach: HVOF spraying deposition of HEA protective coatings
